name: Bombardier Challenger 300/350/3500
summary: The best-selling super-midsize business jet family (1,000 delivered by 2025), a mainstay of US fractional and charter fleets.

wings: Low swept wing with upturned winglets (canted outward on the 350/3500)
engines: Two Honeywell HTF7000-series turbofans in pods high on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Long, slim fuselage that tapers into a long pointed tail cone
tail: T-tail with a swept fin and swept horizontal stabilizer

tellTales: Long, tapering tail cone extending well behind the engines
Upturned winglets and a T-tail on a medium-large twinjet
Rounded-rectangle windows and a long drooped nose

confusedWith.howToTell: Very hard to separate: the Challenger 300/350 cabin tapers into a longer tail cone and its winglets cant outward (350/3500), whereas the Praetor has more upright winglets and a stubbier tail cone ending close behind the engines.
The Challenger 300/350 has rounded-rectangle windows; the G280 has oval windows.
The Challenger 300 is slimmer with a tapering body; the Challenger 600-series has a fat, wide fuselage and a prominent belly fairing.
The Challenger 300/350 has a slim, tapering body with prominent upturned winglets; the Latitude/Longitude has a fat, round fuselage with plain tips or only small winglets.
The G200 has oval windows and a short, thick tail cone; the Challenger 300 has rounded-rectangle windows and a long tapering tail cone.
The Hawker 4000 has plain wingtips with no winglets; the Challenger 300/350 has upturned winglets.
